incident.title: Shipping quotes failing at checkout
symptoms: About 40% of shipping quote requests fail since about 12:00 UTC
Failures eased around 12:30 UTC, then came back
Customers see 'shipping unavailable' and abandon checkout

facts.statement: From about 12:01 UTC shipping-svc POST /quotes returns 502 because parcelhub-api POST /v2/rates returns 429 Too Many Requests. The 429 responses report X-RateLimit-Limit 600/min and X-RateLimit-Remaining 0.
At 11:50 the shipping-svc error rate was 0.3%, with 365 quote requests/min and 370 parcelhub requests/min.
At 12:10 the error rate was 41% and quote requests rose to 1010/min. Parcelhub requests were 600/min, exactly the stated rate limit.
At 12:30 the error rate was 7.5%, with 580 quote requests/min and 540 parcelhub requests/min, which is below the 600/min limit.
At 12:45 the error rate was back to 38% and parcelhub requests were again 600/min. By then the rollback to v5.1.4 had already been deployed (12:27) and started (12:28:05).
marketing-svc v9.4.1 scheduled the Black Week early-access campaign at 11:20. The campaign email went to 1.2M recipients at 11:58.
shipping-svc v5.2.0 (carrier selection) was deployed at 11:55 and started at 11:56:20. It logged an unknown carrier code 'PHX' warning at 12:02:30. It was rolled back to v5.1.4 at 12:27.
At 12:05 the shipping-svc log.level setting was changed from info to debug.
shipping-svc depends on parcelhub-api and address-svc. checkout-web calls shipping-svc.

assumptions.statement: The quote traffic surge came from customers responding to the 1.2M-recipient campaign email.
assumptions.basis: The email went out at 11:58 and quote volume nearly tripled by 12:10. No traffic-source attribution was found.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Check checkout-web or shipping-svc request referrers and UTM parameters, and campaign click-through timing.

assumptions.statement: The dip around 12:30 came from traffic briefly falling below the parcelhub limit, not from the rollback. The return at 12:45 means traffic rose again.
assumptions.basis: The 12:30 quote rate (580/min) is below the limit, but no quote_requests_per_min sample exists for 12:45.

assumptions.statement: There are no matching past incidents. checkout-web metrics returned no data.
assumptions.basis: Both queries returned empty results; coverage may be incomplete.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Query past incidents by tags, and check checkout-web logs directly.

assumptions.statement: shipping-svc makes about one parcelhub call per quote and does not retry 429s.
assumptions.basis: The baseline ratio of parcelhub requests to quote requests is about 1:1, and parcelhub requests are capped at 600 during errors.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Review the shipping-svc parcelhub client's retry and caching settings.

recommended_actions.action: Contact parcelhub to request an emergency temporary increase of the 600/min rate limit, or a burst allowance, for the duration of the Black Week campaign.
recommended_actions.rationale: Quote volume is exceeding parcelhub's 600/min cap. Parcelhub returns 429s, which shipping-svc turns into 502s. Raising the cap removes the bottleneck directly, and error rates track demand against the limit, including the easing around 12:30.

recommended_actions.action: Add short-TTL caching of parcelhub quotes in shipping-svc, keyed by origin, destination and parcel profile, so repeat requests during checkout don't each call parcelhub.
recommended_actions.rationale: Fewer upstream calls keeps volume under the 600/min limit without parcelhub's involvement, and should cut 429-driven failures quickly.

recommended_actions.action: Add client-side rate limiting in shipping-svc toward parcelhub, with jittered retry on 429. When over budget, return a fallback quote (flat-rate or cached estimate) instead of 'shipping unavailable'.
recommended_actions.rationale: Requests over the limit currently surface as hard failures and customers abandon checkout. A degraded but usable quote limits revenue loss while capacity is constrained.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the mechanism: chart per-minute parcelhub call rate against the count of 429 responses and shipping-svc 502s across 11:30–13:00 UTC, and confirm that errors start each time calls reach about 600/min.
recommended_actions.rationale: This confirms the top hypothesis before any mitigation is labeled a fix, and gives a baseline to measure the caching and throttling changes against.

recommended_actions.action: Work with marketing to pace or stagger the Black Week campaign (for example, phased email or push sends) until the parcelhub capacity mitigations are in place. Add upstream third-party quota checks to campaign launch readiness.
recommended_actions.rationale: The campaign roughly 2.8x'd quote volume and is the likely trigger that pushed traffic past parcelhub's limit. Smoothing demand reduces pressure on the cap.

recommended_actions.action: Do not roll back or redeploy shipping-svc further as a remediation. Confirm that error rates after the 12:27 rollback of v5.2.0 match the demand-versus-limit pattern rather than deploy timing.
recommended_actions.rationale: The evidence contradicts the bad-deploy theory: errors returned after the rollback and the failures are upstream 429s. More deploy churn would add risk without addressing the cause.

recommended_actions.action: As low-priority cleanup, revert shipping-svc log.level from debug to its previous level once the incident is stable.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 12:05 debug change is unlikely to be causal; the evidence contradicts it. Reverting it reduces log volume and noise during heavy traffic at very low risk.
